title: O, Say Not, Think Not, Heavenly Notes
description: O, Say Not, Think Not, Heavenly Notes in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Keble wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 443, “Teaching Little Children”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, say not, think not, heav-enly notes To child-ish ears are vain, That the young mind at ran-dom floats, And can-not reach the strain.

lines: O, say not, think not, heavenly notes
To childish ears are vain, —
That the young mind at random floats,
And cannot reach the strain.
Was not our Lord a little child,
Taught by degrees to pray,
By father dear and mother mild
Instructed day by day?
And loved he not of heaven to talk
With children in his sight,
To meet them in his daily walk,
And to his arms invite?
And though some tones be weak and low,
What are all prayers beneath,
But cries of babes, that cannot know
Half the deep thought they breathe?
In his own words we Christ adore;
But angels, as we speak,
Higher above our meaning soar
Than we o'er children weak.
And yet his words mean more than they,
And yet he owns their praise;
O, think not that he turns away
From infants' simple lays!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Keble died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Keble (1792–1866), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
